examples.title: Parallel-wire force: COMSOL documentation transferred to FEMM
examples.summary: Generate and solve the source circular-wire physical problem in FEMM, retaining an explicit boundary-method replacement and analytic force, balance, mesh and domain checks.
assumptions: Baseline wire radius 0.2 m; centers (-0.5,0) m and (+0.5,0) m; left current +1 A and right current -1 A.
Relative permeability is one and the prescribed static current density is uniform. Planar depth is one meter.
The FEMM domain and mesh are declared numerical transfer settings, not a copy of COMSOL infinite elements.
limitations: This is a vendor-documentation method transfer, not execution or certification of a COMSOL model.
The opening historical ampere-definition narrative is not used as a statement of the current SI definition.
The source reports Maxwell surface-stress and Lorentz methods; the FEMM weighted-stress result retains its different method identity.

nodes.title: Parallel circular wires: COMSOL-to-FEMM force transfer
nodes.description: Reconstruct the two-wire physical problem, use an explicit FEMM exterior approximation, and compare independently computed forces with the analytic mutual-force law.
inputs: Two circular wire sections, signed DC currents and unit permeability
outputs: Native FEMM geometry, mesh, solution and separately assessed force checks
constraints: This is a method transfer; COMSOL infinite elements are replaced explicitly, and the solvers are not treated as interchangeable implementations.

verification.note: Reviewed source-to-FEMM method transfer. Native construction, solve and numerical evidence are recorded per run; this record makes no blanket numerical verification claim.

nodes.title: Two nonintersecting circular wire cross-sections
nodes.description: Place equal circular sections at x=-center_distance/2 and x=+center_distance/2, with y=0. The documented baseline uses radius 0.2 m and center distance 1 m.

parameters.name: center_distance
parameters.description: Distance between the two wire centers.

outputs: Closed circular contours and separate labels
constraints: The planar model represents straight wires with one meter of out-of-plane depth; it does not model finite wire ends.

verification.note: Reviewed source-to-FEMM method transfer. Native construction, solve and numerical evidence are recorded per run; this record makes no blanket numerical verification claim.

construction_steps: Set the left and right centers to (-d/2,0) and (+d/2,0).
Draw each circle with four exact quarter-circle arcs and place a label at each center.

nodes.title: Equal and opposite uniform wire currents
nodes.description: Preserve the source currents +I in the left wire and -I in the right wire. In FEMM, separate one-turn circuits in zero-conductivity, unit-permeability regions implement the prescribed uniform static current distribution.

parameters.name: current
parameters.description: Positive magnitude; circuit signs encode opposite directions.

inputs: Separate wire labels and current magnitude
constraints: The source defines J=I/(pi*r^2); current and current density must retain their distinct units.
No skin effect, Hall effect, resistive voltage drop or wire-end effects are included.

verification.note: Reviewed source-to-FEMM method transfer. Native construction, solve and numerical evidence are recorded per run; this record makes no blanket numerical verification claim.

nodes.title: Finite exterior boundary with explicit sensitivity checks
nodes.description: Replace the source cylindrical infinite-element layer with a remote circular FEMM A=0 boundary. Domain radii 10 m and 20 m are declared transfer settings; they are not dimensions prescribed by COMSOL.

parameters.name: domain_radius
parameters.description: Radius of the finite FEMM exterior boundary.

parameters.name: mesh_scale
parameters.description: Multiplier on the declared FEMM mesh sizes.

inputs: Physical wire bounds, exterior radius and mesh settings
outputs: Finite native exterior and recorded mesh/domain sensitivity
constraints: COMSOL uses outer radius 1.5 m including a 0.5 m infinite-element layer. The FEMM replacement changes the numerical boundary method.
Compare mesh scales 1 and 0.5 and domain radii 10 m and 20 m; do not tune the geometry to a measured force.

verification.note: Reviewed source-to-FEMM method transfer. Native construction, solve and numerical evidence are recorded per run; this record makes no blanket numerical verification claim.

nodes.title: Repulsive mutual force and independent native integrals
nodes.description: For nonintersecting circular wires with uniform opposite currents and unit permeability, compare force per unit length against mu0*I^2/(2*pi*d). Keep left/right direction and transverse residuals. FEMM weighted stress and Lorentz force are reported as separate calculations.
inputs: Solved wire regions, current, spacing and planar depth
outputs: Force vectors, balance residuals and analytic force comparison
constraints: The analytic baseline is 2e-7 N/m at I=1 A and d=1 m.
COMSOL reports surface Maxwell stress and volumetric Lorentz integrals. FEMM weighted stress is an explicitly transferred postprocessing method.
Solver completion and a passing force comparison do not establish universal convergence.

verification.note: Reviewed source-to-FEMM method transfer. Native construction, solve and numerical evidence are recorded per run; this record makes no blanket numerical verification claim.
